clue.text: Harry Carpenter's lost pages in boxing volumes

indicators.note: boxing in the sense of enclosing, so one piece sits inside the other
something lost is gone, so the named letters drop out of the word

parts.note: chippy is British slang for a carpenter
pp is the standard abbreviation for pages
v is short for volume, doubled for the plural

explanation.surface: Boxing commentator Harry Carpenter mislays some pages of his books about the sport.
explanation.walkthrough: Harry Carpenter was the BBC's famous boxing commentator, so 'Harry' reads as a first name; it is the verb. CHIPPY loses PP, and the remaining CHIY holds VV.
explanation.definitionFit: To harry and to chivvy both mean to pester or nag someone into action.

clue.text: Motor at speed in soft top? Hardly

explanation.surface: A motor driven fast with a convertible roof sounds like a sporty car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soft top' is a convertible car, but 'Hardly' turns it round: the definition is a hard top, the shell of a crab or tortoise.
explanation.definitionFit: A carapace is the rigid shell on an animal's back, the opposite of a soft covering.

clue.text: Callous article suppressed by popular philosopher

indicators.note: something suppressed is held down inside, so one piece is enclosed by the other

explanation.surface: A popular thinker silences a piece of writing he dislikes.
explanation.definitionFit: Callous behaviour is cruel and unfeeling, lacking human compassion.

clue.text: Most gutsy, ejecting supporter before a match

indicators.note: before places one piece ahead of the next in the answer
ejecting throws something out, so those letters leave the word

parts.note: a bra is a supporting undergarment

explanation.surface: The bravest player is sent off a supporter just before a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'match' looks like a sporting fixture; it is the thing you strike. BRAVEST without BRA leaves VEST.
explanation.definitionFit: A vesta is a short wax match, named after the Roman goddess of the hearth.

clue.text: Work on second at Oxford, drinking a lot

indicators.note: drinking takes something in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a lot in the sense of frequently
a student in residence at university is said to be up

explanation.surface: A second-year Oxford student studies hard while drinking heavily.
explanation.definitionFit: To soften someone up is to work on them, wearing down resistance before a request.

clue.text: Extreme response from more than one class in school conflict

parts.note: RE is religious education, a school lesson

explanation.surface: A playground fight drawing in several classes provokes a heavy-handed reaction.
explanation.walkthrough: RE, religious education, is a subject on the British school timetable.
explanation.definitionFit: An overreaction is a response out of proportion, an excessive reply to events.

clue.text: He got trim woven for a producer of woolly bears

indicators.note: weaving interlaces threads into a new pattern, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man gets some trimming woven to make a knitter's woolly toy bears.
explanation.walkthrough: Woolly bears are hairy caterpillars, not teddies.
explanation.definitionFit: The tiger moth's caterpillar is the furry larva commonly nicknamed a woolly bear.

clue.text: A Christie novel has an added French dialect

indicators.note: added means put on after, so the second piece follows the first

parts.note: N or M? is an Agatha Christie novel

explanation.surface: An Agatha Christie mystery comes with an extra passage in French.
explanation.definitionFit: Norman French was the dialect of Normandy, spoken in England after the Conquest.

clue.text: At the end stir in sauce very quickly

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: pesto is an Italian basil sauce

indicators.note: at the end points to the final letter of the next word only

explanation.surface: A cooking instruction: finally stir the sauce in very fast.
explanation.definitionFit: Presto is the musical direction for a very fast tempo.

clue.text: Recycled material this chap turned into hives?

indicators.note: into places one piece inside the other
turned round means the letters run the other way

explanation.surface: A man turns old stuff into beehives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hives' suggests bee homes; it is the itchy skin condition.
explanation.definitionFit: A rehash is old material reused with little change, a noun for something recycled.

clue.text: Dish that's sharp mostly fed unnatural greed

indicators.note: being fed takes something in, so one piece goes inside
mostly means not quite all, so the final letter is cut

parts.note: keen means sharp, as of a blade

indicators.note: unnatural means not in its normal form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A spicy dish greedily overeaten seems the unnatural result of gluttony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sharp' and 'fed' read like adjectives about a person; one is the outer word, docked of its tail, the other says it swallows the reworked letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Kedgeree is an Anglo-Indian dish of rice, smoked fish and eggs.

clue.text: Score over half a century, say

definitions.text: Score over half a century, say

parts.note: surface reading: a cricketer making more than fifty runs

parts.words: Score over half a century, say
parts.note: setter's reading: twenty over fifty, a fraction to be expressed as a proportion of a hundred

explanation.walkthrough: A score is twenty and half a century is fifty; 'over' is the fraction line, so twenty divided by fifty, and 'say' flags a value given as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Twenty out of fifty equals two fifths, which as a proportion of a hundred is this figure.

clue.text: Mop up road spills in High Barnet

indicators.note: spilt things scatter in disorder, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Clearing up road spills in High Barnet, a north London suburb.
explanation.walkthrough: High Barnet is a London place name, but barnet is rhyming slang (Barnet Fair) for hair, so a high barnet is a tall hairdo.
explanation.definitionFit: A pompadour is a hairstyle swept high off the forehead, so it is lofty hair.

clue.text: Get too hot while slicing baloney

parts.note: as in the sense of during

explanation.definitionFit: To roast in everyday speech is to be uncomfortably hot, as on a sweltering day.

clue.text: Something used to focus or intensify a concert not working right

definitions.text: Something used to focus or intensify

indicators.note: working here means being worked over, kneaded into a new shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.walkthrough: 'not working' reads as one phrase meaning broken, but 'not' belongs to the fodder and 'working' alone signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: A concentrator is a device that strengthens or condenses something, such as a solar concentrator focusing light.

clue.text: Cut in diet originally due to nuts

explanation.surface: A dieter cut out nuts at the start of a regime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'originally' looks like a first-letter signal but no single letter is taken; the full words diet and due to supply the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Edited out means removed in editing, a past participle meaning cut from a text or film.

clue.text: Outside US city, dismal saloon provides stop-off for diners

indicators.note: outside means wrapped around, so one piece encloses the other

explanation.surface: A dreary saloon on the edge of an American city where travellers stop to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: A salad bar is a counter where diners help themselves to salads.

clue.text: Home again, engineers sat on wooden bench

indicators.note: in a down entry, sitting on means placed above, so the first piece comes before

parts.note: a settle is a high-backed wooden bench

explanation.surface: Soldiers back home sit on a wooden bench.
explanation.walkthrough: The Royal Engineers is a British army corps, abbreviated RE.
explanation.definitionFit: To resettle is to give a new home or move back into one, used as a verb.

clue.text: Murder trial documents found here

explanation.surface: The evidence in a murder trial is kept here.
explanation.definitionFit: A dispatch case is a briefcase for carrying papers, so official papers would be stored in it.

clue.text: More work about opiates covered up

explanation.definitionFit: Utopia is Thomas More's 1516 book about an ideal island society.

clue.text: Cod's wasted in rubbish batter

parts.note: taken as written, the letters to remove

explanation.walkthrough: 'batter' looks like the fish coating; it is the verb meaning to hit.
explanation.definitionFit: To wallop is to hit hard, the same as to batter someone.

clue.text: Guy taking time to relax

indicators.note: taking means picking up the next piece to follow on

explanation.surface: A man takes some time off to unwind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guy' looks like a man; it is the verb meaning to mock.
explanation.definitionFit: To guy someone is to make fun of them, which is to tease.

clue.text: View of skyline or of space for rebuilding

indicators.note: rebuilding puts something together anew, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Talk of a skyline view, or of space that could be redeveloped.
explanation.definitionFit: A roofscape is the visual scene formed by a town's rooftops, the outline against the sky.

clue.text: Wrap, possibly with fur ripped off

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a shoulder scarf, often of fur

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a fur garment being torn; the second meaning is the past tense of steal.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a noun for a shawl worn over the shoulders and the past tense of theft.

clue.text: Top drivers may do this at lay-bys

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a knitted upper garment

definitions.text: drivers may do this at lay-bys
definitions.meaning: second meaning: what motorists do when stopping at the roadside

explanation.walkthrough: A lay-by is a British roadside stopping place; read as two words, the answer is what motorists do there.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a sweater, a knitted garment, and as a phrasal verb means to stop at the roadside.

clue.text: Sweet place to hold the Royal Ball

parts.note: the orb is the jewelled ball in the royal regalia

clue.text: Bishop finally admitted to a slight thirst

clue.text: Last time transport picks up close to home

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so only the last letter is used
